judged_text: saveChanges() calls this.get('embedding').update({}) with no rejection handler, and the server action it targets (Admin::EmbeddingController#update) persists nothing — it only re-serializes the fetched records. If this action is ever wired to a save button (its name and RESTful PUT route strongly suggest it), a failure surfaces as an unhandled rejection, and a success response falsely reports that changes were saved when the endpoint wrote nothing to the database; the actual persistence path is the per-host save() in the component, so the controller-level 'save' is a success-reporting no-op.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defining `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` with no `.catch(...)`, and the corresponding server `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-serializes `@embedding` without persisting anything. However, the new `embedding.hbs` template does not wire any button/action to `saveChanges` (it only has per-host save/delete via the `embeddable-host` component and an `addHost` button), so there is no verifiable broken behavior in the UI as added here—it's more of a misleading/dead RESTful “save” endpoint/action that could cause unhandled rejections or no-op saves if later hooked up.
